predecessors.name: Ma Chu
predecessors.text: the former Chu territory ('present-day Hunan and northeastern Guangxi' for the Ma Chu; the Wuping circuit held its Hunan part)

predecessors.name: Southern Tang
predecessors.text: Hunan, held by the Southern Tang from 951 until Bian Hao fled Tanzhou on 1 December 952

successors.name: Song dynasty (Northern and Southern Song)
successors.text: the former Chu territory ('present-day Hunan and northeastern Guangxi' for the Ma Chu; the Wuping circuit held its Hunan part)

ledger.x: 952: Chu generals rise and the Wuping circuit begins.
952: former Chu troops attack the Southern Tang across Hunan.
1 December 952: Hunan passes from the Southern Tang to the former Chu generals.
963: the Song seize Hunan and the Wuping circuit ends.

wars.name: Southern Tang conquest of Chu and the Hunan rebellion
wars.outcome: The Southern Tang subjugated Chu in 951, but 'much of the state was lost in a rebellion against the deeply unpopular Southern Tang administration'; Bian Hao fled Tanzhou on 1 December 952 and Hunan passed to the former Chu generals.

wars.name: Song campaign against Jingnan and Wuping
wars.outcome: The Song army, sent against Zhang Wenbiao's rebellion in Wuping, took Jiangling without a fight and the Wuping Jiedushi was ended in 963.

certainty.note: No boundary is recorded: Hunan's modern outline stands for the circuit; the Guangxi side and the Jingnan frontier are not given by any page opened.
